What is not a statement of one of Newton’s laws of motion?

options.A: If body X exerts a force on body Y, body Y exerts an equal and opposite force on body X.
options.B: If no resultant force acts on a body it has constant velocity.
options.C: The rate of change of momentum of a body is proportional to the resultant force acting on it and takes place in the direction of the force.
options.D: The total momentum of a system of interacting bodies is constant if there is no external force.

A beam of α-particles is incident on a thin gold foil. One α-particle collides head-on with a gold
nucleus and is deflected back along its original path.
Which statement could explain why the recoil speed of the gold nucleus is small compared with
the recoil speed of the α-particle?

options.A: Most α-particles are only slightly deflected as they pass through the gold foil.
options.B: The α-particle and the gold nucleus repel each other.
options.C: The mass of the gold nucleus is much greater than the mass of the α-particle.
options.D: The momentum of the α-particle decreases as it approaches the gold nucleus.

An object is moving along the ground in a straight line at a constant speed.
Which statement about the resultant force acting on the object is correct?

options.A: The resultant force acting on the object is equal to its weight.
options.B: The resultant force acting on the object is equal to the product of its mass and its velocity.
options.C: The resultant force acting on the object is equal to the resistive force.
options.D: The resultant force acting on the object is equal to zero.
